question: Smith (2017a): the tables that illustrate single changes with lexemes, and the inventories of the language sketches (gap audit of 26 November 2026). What is entered from them?
chosen_reading: Only what the rows of batch smith2017-borneo did not yet say. New lects from tables with a variety that was not a lect: Aoheng (aohe1238, Tables 44-48), Punan Lisum (no Glottocode) and Buket (buka1261, Tables 32, 34), Siang (sian1254, Table 82), each with only the rows those tables state and the rest assumed unchanged. Rows added to existing lects: the lowering of initial high vowels and of *-iʔ from *-ak in Kereho and Seputan, and PMÜL *-ak > *-i(ʔ) (Tables 46-47); penultimate schwa after *p, *b and penultimate *a in Hliboi, Sungkung, Jangkang, Ribun, Golik and Sanggau, read off Table 53 with counts; vowel breaking after *a in Ketapang, Seberuang, Iban and Mualang (Table 61) as an inserted glide plus a vowel change; sporadic *-h > ʔ (Table 63) and Iban diphthongization (Tables 64-65). Sourced inventories: Hliboi (Tables 54-55, j entered as ɟ) and Kelai (Tables 19-20). Punan Bah's off-glide vowels are entered as allophones (Table 36) beside the existing rows that have them as reflexes. Not entered: the Merap inventory (Tables 12-13), because the Merap rows from Smith (2017b) use symbols the table does not have; Biatah, Bukar-Sadong and Singai (Table 53), Lepo' Tau and Lepo' Sawa' (Table 81) and Western Penan (Tables 89-90), which are not lects; Table 79; Table 88 (Proto-Central Sarawak is held back). Kadorih *z (Tables 82-83) is left as it is: see the alternatives.
alternatives: Enter no lect from a lexeme table; or copy Seputan's rows to Aoheng; or give Punan Lisum lisu1251. Replace the off-glide reflex rows of Punan Bah by the plain vowels. Respell the existing Hliboi row *z > d͡ʒ as ɟ, and the Kelai rows with aj, aw, aːe̯, j, which are outside the sourced inventories. For Kadorih, mark the rows *z > d͡ʒ as borrowed from Ngaju (loan-stratum): Smith argues that *z became c and that j is secondary (pp. 279-280).
